                     Public Utility Commission of Texas

                                        Memorandum


 TO:             Chairman Thomas J. Gleeson
                 Commissioner Kathleen Jackson
                 Commissioner Courtney K. Hjaltman
                 Commissioner Morgan Johnson
                 Commissioner Patrick Rhode

 FROM:           Werner Roth, Senior Market Economist
                 Market Analysis Division

 DATE:           April 30, 2026

 RE:             May 7, 2026 Open Meeting, Agenda Item No. 29
                 Project No. 58777 – Triennial Reliability Assessment for the ERCOT Region
                 Under §25.508
                 Staff Memo on CONE Reference Technology and Timelines


At the Commission’s April 17, 2026 open meeting, Staff committed to come back to this open
meeting to receive guidance on the two remaining open items:

   •   A revised recommendation on the technology reference for the ERCOT Cost of New
       Entry (CONE) review
   •   A revised timeline that accounts for the additional time needed to review the load
       forecast
CONE Reference Technology

Staff originally recommended that ERCOT use the small frame combustion turbine as the
reference technology for its limited CONE study. 1 This aligned with ERCOT’s
recommendation in its March 23rd filing. 2 Though it was more expensive than the larger frame
combustion turbine historically used for previous ERCOT CONE values, it represented a
technology that was considered more likely to be available by 2029. 3 Staff noted the increased
uncertainty around the near-term availability of any additional natural gas generation beyond
what has already been procured and recommended that the CONE value used to inform market
design changes should not be based on short-term, abnormal conditions, but on what the market

   1
     Project No. 58777, AIS Item 37 (Staff's Final Recommendation on Reliability Standard Assessment and
   CONE Assumptions) at 2-3.
   2
     Project No. 58777, AIS Item 35 (ERCOT's Final Recommendation of Modeling Assumptions and
   CONE Study for the 2026 Reliability Assessment) at 5.
   3
     A previous Staff memo (Project No. 58777, AIS Item 37) mistakenly implied that prior CONE studies
   performed for the ERCOT region examined a small frame combustion turbine. Staff subsequently
   identified this error and has confirmed that the most recent CONE study used a large frame CT as the
   reference technology.

                                                 Page 1 of 2
 is trying to incentivize long-term to satisfy the reliability standard. 4 After additional
consideration and discussion, Staff now believes that the more appropriate choice of reference
technology is the large frame combustion turbine that has historically been used to set the
ERCOT CONE value, rather than the more expensive small frame combustion turbine. Any
modification to the reference technology can be considered prior to the next reliability standard
assessment in 2029.

Additionally, Staff had recommended that the CONE value be reported in real dollars, 5 as this
is consistent with how CONE has been previously reported in ERCOT. Upon further
consideration, Staff modifies this recommendation to have ERCOT and its consultant report
CONE values in both real and nominal dollars and summarize the pros and cons of using
either value in setting ERCOT’s CONE.

Updated Timeline

On December 11, 2025, Staff filed a memo 6 with timelines to complete the reliability standard
assessment. Based on discussions at the April 17, 2026 open meeting, Staff is requesting
guidance on how to incorporate the load forecast review and adjustment process into these
timelines. Staff is prepared to bring back a revised timeline that reflects this guidance and
discussion to the May 29, 2026 open meeting.

Next Steps

Staff will file a short memo in this project memorializing open meeting discussions on the
reliability standard assessment assumptions, including any decisions made on the CONE
reference technology.
